name: Nuxt.js
tagline: The server-rendered reactor core for advanced web architectures.
timeTravelLog: Launched in 2016 by Sebastien Chopin to bring Server-Side Rendering (SSR) and automated file-based routing to Vue.js interfaces, reducing config overhead to near zero.
overview: Nuxt.js is an open-source framework that makes web development intuitive and powerful. It handles SSR, static generation, file-system routing, and modular plugin architecture — all with zero manual configuration.

syllabus.title: Module 1: File-System Routing (Pages Directory)
syllabus.desc: How Nuxt automatically converts files into routable URL endpoints.
syllabus.content: Nuxt eliminates manual router configuration. Every .vue file inside the pages/ directory automatically becomes a web route. The file name defines the path: pages/index.vue → /, pages/about.vue → /about, pages/ship/engine.vue → /ship/engine. Nested directories create nested routes.
syllabus.interactiveTip: Use <NuxtLink> instead of <a> for internal navigation in Nuxt — it handles client-side routing with prefetching, making navigation instant without full page reloads!

syllabus.title: Module 2: Server-Side Rendering (SSR)
syllabus.desc: Pre-assembling complete HTML pages on the server for speed and SEO.
syllabus.content: By default, Nuxt renders pages on the server first, sending complete HTML to the browser. This means search engines receive fully structured content immediately, dramatically improving SEO. The page then 'hydrates' — becoming interactive client-side. This contrasts with SPAs where the browser receives an empty shell and must execute JS before rendering.
syllabus.interactiveTip: Use <ClientOnly> to wrap components that rely on browser-only APIs (like window, localStorage, or WebGL) — this prevents hydration mismatches that cause console errors!

syllabus.title: Module 3: Dynamic Routes (Bracket Syntax)
syllabus.desc: Building routes that respond to dynamic ID parameters.
syllabus.content: Dynamic route segments are defined using square brackets in the filename. pages/ship/[id].vue creates a route matching /ship/anything — the id value is extracted as a route parameter. useRoute().params.id reads the active parameter value inside the component.
syllabus.interactiveTip: Wrap dynamic segments in double brackets [[id]] to make the parameter optional. This creates a catch-all route that also matches the parent path without a parameter!

syllabus.title: Module 4: Shared Layouts (layouts/ Directory)
syllabus.desc: Building consistent page shells with shared headers, sidebars, and footers.
syllabus.content: Nuxt's layouts/ directory defines reusable page wrappers. The default layout (layouts/default.vue) wraps every page automatically. Custom layouts can be applied per-page using definePageMeta. <NuxtPage /> (or <slot /> inside layouts) renders the page content inside the layout shell.
syllabus.codeExample: // layouts/default.vue // pages/about.vue — uses custom layout
syllabus.interactiveTip: To opt out of the default layout on a specific page, set definePageMeta({ layout: false }) in the page script. You can then apply your own full-page container directly.

syllabus.title: Module 5: Module Plugins & Configuration (nuxt.config.ts)
syllabus.desc: Extending Nuxt capabilities with zero-config module integrations.
syllabus.content: Nuxt's module system enables powerful features via single-line installations. Modules handle bundler configuration, auto-imports, and plugin registration behind the scenes. Popular modules include @pinia/nuxt (global state), @nuxt/image (optimized images), @nuxtjs/tailwindcss, and @nuxt/ui.
syllabus.interactiveTip: Use useRuntimeConfig() inside components to safely access environment variables at runtime — never hardcode API keys or sensitive values in component scripts!

syllabus.title: Module 6: Server API Routes (server/api/)
syllabus.desc: Writing full-stack backend endpoints directly inside the Nuxt project.
syllabus.content: Nuxt provides a server/ directory that uses Nitro under the hood. Files inside server/api/ automatically become HTTP API endpoints. Server routes run only on the server — perfect for secure database queries, API proxies, or authentication logic that should never be exposed to the client browser.
syllabus.interactiveTip: Use useFetch('/api/missions') in your Vue components to call server API routes. Nuxt handles SSR data fetching, deduplication, and client-side updates automatically!

syllabus.title: Module 7: Production Build & Deployment
syllabus.desc: Building and deploying your Nuxt application for the live universe.
syllabus.content: Nuxt supports multiple output modes: SSR (Node.js server), static generation (HTML files for CDN hosting), and edge rendering. nuxt build compiles SSR output. nuxt generate pre-renders all pages as static files. nuxi preview serves the built output locally for final checks before launch.
syllabus.codeExample:
# Development server
npx nuxi dev

# Build for SSR (Node.js server output)
npx nuxi build

# Static generation (HTML for CDN / GitHub Pages)
npx nuxi generate

# Preview the production build locally
npx nuxi preview
syllabus.interactiveTip: For static GitHub Pages deployment, use nuxt generate and deploy the .output/public directory. For Vercel or Netlify, the SSR build deploys automatically with zero config!

quiz.question: How does Nuxt generate routes for your application?
options: By parsing a routes.json config file
Automatically from .vue files placed in the pages/ directory
Through manual import declarations in main.js
Via a regular expression module in the server config
quiz.explanation: Nuxt uses file-system routing — every .vue file in the pages/ directory automatically becomes a route. No manual router configuration is ever needed.

quiz.question: What is the advantage of Server-Side Rendering (SSR) for SEO?
options: The server stores pages in a faster database
Search engine crawlers receive complete HTML immediately, not an empty JS shell
SSR removes all images to reduce page weight
It locks content behind login so it is not indexed
quiz.explanation: With SSR, search engine bots receive fully rendered HTML on first request. SPAs send an empty HTML shell that bots often cannot fully execute, severely limiting SEO visibility.

quiz.question: How do you create a dynamic route in Nuxt that accepts an 'id' parameter?
options: Add id to the nuxt.config routes array
quiz.explanation: Square bracket syntax [id] in the filename creates a dynamic route segment. The parameter value is accessible via useRoute().params.id inside the component.
